claims.text: Six hours of high-energy ball milling induces high lattice strain in CoCrFeNiTi powder.
Six hours of high-energy ball milling refines CoCrFeNiTi to a nanocrystalline grain size.
The strain and grain refinement produced by milling lower the activation-energy barrier for an FCC-to-BCC solid-solution transition.
VEC and atomic-radius mismatch govern the FCC/BCC phase stability of CoCrFeNiTi.
After six hours of milling, the CoCrFeNiTi powder is a metastable FCC solid solution.
SPS at 1000°C provides sufficient diffusion for near-theoretical densification of the milled CoCrFeNiTi powder.
SPS at 1000°C activates the transition from metastable FCC to BCC in milled CoCrFeNiTi.
SPS at 1000°C with a short dwell is insufficient to cause substantial Ti-rich HCP precipitation.
SPS at 1000°C with a short dwell avoids significant grain coarsening.
Ball milling increases the configurational entropy of CoCrFeNiTi and thereby assists the FCC/BCC transition.
Ball milling raises the internal energy of CoCrFeNiTi and lowers the kinetic barrier to its FCC/BCC transition.
A VEC below 6.87 together with high atomic-radius mismatch favors the BCC state in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed milling and SPS route will produce CoCrFeNiTi at greater than 98% theoretical density.
The resulting microstructure will be BCC-dominant, either single-phase BCC or dual-phase FCC/BCC.
Nanocrystalline grain-boundary strengthening will increase the Vickers hardness of the SPS alloy.
Lattice distortion and solid-solution hardening will contribute to the increased hardness.
The SPS alloy will have lower porosity than cast CoCrFeNiTi.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has low hardness, high porosity, and may contain segregated brittle intermetallic phases.
Temperatures above 1050°C or dwell times above 30 minutes cause excessive HCP precipitation or grain coarsening that degrades mechanical properties.
Vickers testing at a 100 g load can isolate grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening.
